moat_against: Commoditized products, transparent pricing: ~21-22% gross and ~5-6% operating margins show no durable pricing power
Powerful counterparties: giant suppliers and hyperscaler/utility customers with procurement leverage
Low switching costs on product-only share; regional distributors and direct channels contest share
Moat carried in working capital and a $5,781.4M net-debt stack, not intangibles — growth must be funded
moat_for: Distribution scale: ~$23.5B sales, ~700 sites in ~50 countries, millions of SKUs
Integrated supply / VMI / project services (One Wesco) embed Wesco in customer operations; backlog up ~60% YoY
Data-center solutions position across CSS, EES and UBS tied to the AI capex cycle
Premier-supplier breadth and fill-rate reliability in project work
moat_justification: Real scale and service-embedding advantages in a business whose ~5-6% operating margins and commodity product mix prove pricing power is limited; equally scaled rivals (Graybar, Ferguson, Grainger, Rexel) contest the same national accounts. Scale (~$23.5B sales, ~700 sites, millions of SKUs), integrated-supply/VMI embedding and a cross-all-three-segments data-center position argue moderate; commoditized products, powerful suppliers and hyperscaler/utility customers, low switching costs on product-only wallet share, and a moat carried in working capital and debt rather than intangibles cap it at narrow/moderate.
name: WESCO International, Inc.
one_liner: Real scale distributor riding the data-center cycle, moat 5/10 — but owner's earnings were positive in only 2 of the last 5 years because growth consumes its working capital; at $346.01 it yields a 5.63% weighted IRR with IV@15% of $79.51 and clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$79.51.
